html:
Alash Orda was the government of the Alash Autonomy, a Kazakh national state proclaimed in December 1917 after the Russian Revolution and lasting until 1920. Its centre was at Semey, then called Semipalatinsk.

It was led by the Alash party of educated Kazakhs: Alikhan Bokeikhanov, the poet Akhmet Baitursynov, who reformed the Kazakh alphabet, and others. They wanted land rights for Kazakhs against Russian settlers and a modern Kazakh nation within a democratic Russia. In the Russian Civil War they first sided with the Whites, then with the Bolsheviks.

The Bolsheviks dissolved it in 1920. Many of its leaders served in the early Soviet republic, then were killed in Stalin's Great Purge in 1937 and 1938. Banned for decades, they were honoured after independence as founders of Kazakhstan.
